Quantum annealers' primary objective is to solve hard computational optimization problems. Because these optimization problems are in the NP-Hard complexity class, they are of great interest in several fields. One of the leading open questions concerning quantum annealers asks whether they will outperform other classical methods for solving these problems; Some aspects of this question are addressed in this thesis. The first part of the thesis investigates whether quantum annealing provides improved performance for solving a particular family of NP problems, called the Quadratic Knapsack Problem (QKP), using the D-Wave Quantum Annealer. The performance metrics used to assess QKP solving are the solution quality and the total runtime, and are benchmarked against other classical solvers. \\\\n \\\\nFurthermore, we extend our research on quantum annealers to propose two use cases for such systems. One is for Blockchain technology, and the second is in the area of quantum chaos. For the first use case of QA, an application for Blockchain's Proof of Work (PoW) is proposed, based on having hard optimization problems as an alternative to PoW hashing challenge, and using quantum annealers as solvers. For the second use case of QA, we propose simulating quantum chaos on the D-Wave Quantum Annealer to study the transition between the deep quantum realm and the classical limit in a chaotic system, and obtain insights into the “quantumness\\\" of quantum annealers.\"}, {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W7211866405\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.1177/14705931261480400\", \"title\": \"The promise of dwelling – Affective encounters with ‘not yet’ data\", \"publication_year\": 2026, \"type\": \"article\", \"cited_by_count\": 0, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"hybrid\", \"oa_url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1177/14705931261480400\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"doi:10.1177/14705931261480400\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.1177/14705931261480400\", \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1177/14705931261480400\", \"pdf_url\": null, \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S195188575\", \"display_name\": \"Marketing Theory\", \"issn_l\": \"1470-5931\", \"issn\": [\"1470-5931\", \"1741-301X\"], \"is_oa\": false, \"is_in_doaj\": false, \"is_core\": true, \"listed_in\": [\"abdc-a\", \"anvur-class-a\", \"anvur-scientific\", \"cwts-core\", \"erih-plus\", \"fnege-3\", \"jufo-2\", \"norway-1\", \"poland-100\", \"russia-white-list-1\"], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/P4310320017\", \"host_organization_name\": \"SAGE Publishing\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/P4310320017\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [\"SAGE Publishing\"], \"type\": \"journal\"}, \"license\": \"cc-by\", \"license_id\": \"https://openalex.org/licenses/cc-by\", \"version\": \"publishedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": true, \"is_published\": true, \"raw_source_name\": \"Marketing Theory\", \"raw_type\": \"journal-article\"}, \"abstract\": \"Research on affective encounters is necessarily embodied and entangled with elusive, often affect-drenched data. In this paper, we show how our study of Zagreb’s Museum of Broken Relationships benefited from methodological innovations in organisational studies involving affective ethnography and ‘not-yet’ data. Drawing on the theorising of Martin Heidegger, we also reflect on our attempts to dwell in elusive, more-than-representational data through the use of multimodal arts-based methods: writing with resonance, poetry and illustration. We suggest that our poetic dwelling illuminated and helped materialise the immaterial, fostering an affective form of sensemaking concerning the spatial, temporal and material intensities of affective encounters. We reflect on the promise of dwelling in data for analysing differently, knowing differently, and researching differently within and beyond highly-charged atmospheres such as our context.\"}, {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W4410492287\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevx.15.021059\", \"title\": \"Measurement-Induced Entanglement and Complexity in Random Constant-Depth 2D Quantum Circuits\", \"publication_year\": 2025, \"type\": \"article\", \"cited_by_count\": 6, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"gold\", \"oa_url\": \"http://link.aps.org/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021059\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"doi:10.1103/physrevx.15.021059\", \"doi\": \"https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevx.15.021059\", \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevx.15.021059\", \"pdf_url\": \"http://link.aps.org/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021059\", \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S137042341\", \"display_name\": \"Physical Review X\", \"issn_l\": \"2160-3308\", \"issn\": [\"2160-3308\"], \"is_oa\": true, \"is_in_doaj\": true, \"is_core\": true, \"listed_in\": [\"cwts-core\", \"doaj\", \"dongbi-a\", \"jufo-3\", \"ki-jl-2\", \"norway-2\", \"poland-200\", \"russia-white-list-1\"], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/P4310320261\", \"host_organization_name\": \"American Physical Society\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/P4310320261\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [\"American Physical Society\"], \"type\": \"journal\"}, \"license\": \"cc-by\", \"license_id\": \"https://openalex.org/licenses/cc-by\", \"version\": \"publishedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": true, \"is_published\": true, \"raw_source_name\": \"Physical Review X\", \"raw_type\": \"journal-article\"}, \"abstract\": \"We analyze the entanglement structure of states generated by random constant-depth two-dimensional quantum circuits, followed by projective measurements of a subset of sites. By deriving a rigorous lower bound on the average entanglement entropy of such postmeasurement states, we prove that macroscopic long-ranged entanglement is generated above some constant critical depth in several natural classes of circuit architectures, which include brickwork circuits and random holographic tensor networks. This behavior had been conjectured based on previous works, which utilize nonrigorous methods such as replica theory calculations, or work in regimes where the local Hilbert space dimension grows with system size. To establish our lower bound, we develop new replica-free theoretical techniques that leverage tools from multiuser quantum information theory, which are of independent interest, allowing us to map the problem onto a statistical mechanics model of self-avoiding walks without requiring large local Hilbert space dimension. Our findings have consequences for the complexity of classically simulating sampling from random shallow circuits and of contracting tensor networks. First, we show that standard algorithms based on matrix product states which are used for both these tasks will fail above some constant depth and bond dimension, respectively. In addition, we also prove that these random constant-depth quantum circuits cannot be simulated by any classical circuit of sublogarithmic depth.\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "274a3391be61fb996e4ca82797395cd7471c828a25311bc09cd1efeaf6480101", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "scrambling_records", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1177/14705931261480400", "doi:10.1103/physrevx.15.021059", "openalex:W3202960440", "openalex:W7211866405", "openalex:W4410492287"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1177/14705931261480400", "https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevx.15.021059"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
